settings.privacy.drm.title: Pause for DRM & Remote Desktop
settings.privacy.drm.tooltip: pauses all screen capture when a DRM-protected streaming app (netflix, disney+, hulu, prime video, apple tv, etc.) or a remote-desktop client (Omnissa/VMware Horizon) is focused. these apps blank their windows when any app is recording the screen — pausing capture while they're focused keeps them usable. capture resumes automatically when you switch away.
settings.privacy.drm.description: Avoid DRM black screens (Netflix, Disney+) and gray Horizon windows.
settings.privacy.clipboard.title: Capture clipboard
settings.privacy.clipboard.tooltip: when on, screenpipe records clipboard copy/paste events and contents. turn off if you ship ~/.screenpipe to a remote LLM or share it — passwords, API keys, and private keys frequently pass through the clipboard.
settings.privacy.clipboard.description: Skip if your data leaves the machine (passwords, keys often pass through copy/paste).
settings.privacy.keyboard.title: Capture keyboard
settings.privacy.keyboard.tooltip: when on, screenpipe records what you type (your keystrokes). off by default. the accessibility tree and OCR still capture on-screen text either way, so Rewind and Ask keep working — this only controls the raw keystroke stream, where passwords, API keys, and secrets you type would otherwise be logged.
settings.privacy.keyboard.description: Off by default. Records the raw keystroke stream (secrets often get typed). On-screen text is still captured.
settings.privacy.clicks.title: Capture clicks
settings.privacy.clicks.tooltip: when on, screenpipe records mouse click events (where and what you clicked). on by default — clicks carry no text payload and power workflow analysis and task mining. turning this off only skips the click rows; clicks still trigger screen captures.
settings.privacy.clicks.description: On by default. Click events power workflow analysis; no text is recorded.
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.title: Input Monitoring permission
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.tooltip: macOS permission that lets screenpipe capture keystrokes and mouse clicks. without it, capture runs in reduced mode — clipboard and app/window switches still work, but keyboard and click recording is dropped.
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.intro: Lets screenpipe capture keystrokes and mouse clicks. Optional — clipboard and app/window switches still work without it. Grant this only if you want a full input replay (Pi can search what you typed and where you clicked).
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.hint1: If the prompt doesn't appear, toggle
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.hint2: on in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring. Relaunch screenpipe after enabling — macOS only applies TCC changes on next process start.
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.ghost1: Permission could not be activated after requesting it. Toggle
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.ghost2: on in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring. If the toggle is already on but capture still fails, click
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.ghost3: to clear a stale TCC record and re-request.
settings.privacy.inputMonitoring.restart: to start capturing keystrokes and clicks. The running recorder was started without Input Monitoring and won't pick up the change until next launch.
settings.privacy.recordLocked.title: Record Audio While Locked
settings.privacy.recordLocked.tooltip: when enabled, audio recording continues even when your screen is locked. by default, audio recording pauses when the screen is locked to save resources and protect privacy.
settings.privacy.recordLocked.descriptio: Continue audio capture when screen is locked
settings.privacy.pii.title: PII Removal
settings.privacy.pii.tooltip: Redacts emails, phones, secrets, and more from captures. Smart mode adds names, addresses, and image redaction.
settings.privacy.pii.state.off: Off — captures store raw text and pixels.
settings.privacy.pii.state.basic: Basic — regex on capture. Emails, phones, SSNs, cards, API keys.
settings.privacy.pii.state.smart: Smart — AI background worker. Adds names, addresses, image redaction.
settings.privacy.pii.basic.label: Basic
settings.privacy.pii.basic.desc: — regex on capture. Free, instant, deterministic. Catches emails, phones, SSNs, cards, JWTs, API keys, private keys, connection strings.
settings.privacy.pii.smart.label: Smart
settings.privacy.pii.smart.desc: — includes Basic, plus an AI background worker for semantic PII (names, addresses, sensitive context) and image redaction on screen frames. Downloads a ~100 MB model on first run.
settings.privacy.pii.text.label: Text
settings.privacy.pii.text.desc: — scrub captured text (OCR, accessibility, transcripts, typed & clipboard input)
settings.privacy.pii.image.label: Images
settings.privacy.pii.image.desc: — black out PII in screenshot frames (on-device vision model)
settings.privacy.pii.backend.description: Local stays on-device — strongest privacy, slower on weak hardware. Cloud uses screenpipe's attested confidential-compute enclave — fast everywhere; your device verifies the open-source build before sending anything.
settings.privacy.pii.unselectedNote: Unselected types stay visible so your timeline remains searchable. Secrets are always removed in both modes.
settings.privacy.pii.whereWeLook.descrip: We always scan what you type, your clipboard, transcripts, window titles, and on-screen text. Turn on any of these extra places the same info can hide — hover a row to see what it covers.
settings.privacy.pii.pseudonyms.label: Consistent pseudonyms
settings.privacy.pii.pseudonyms.desc1: — replace each value with a stable token like
settings.privacy.pii.pseudonyms.desc3: , so the same person or value stays linkable across your timeline without being exposed. One-way and on-device — the original can't be recovered. Applies to newly-recorded activity going forward.
settings.privacy.agentLogs.label: Redact secrets in agent logs
settings.privacy.agentLogs.desc: — coding agents (Pi) save full sessions, including any passwords, API keys, or tokens they touch, in plaintext on disk. When on, a background worker strips secrets from idle agent session logs. Secrets-only and on-device; never rewrites a session a run is still using.
settings.privacy.analytics.title: Analytics
settings.privacy.analytics.tooltip: Product usage events only — features used, errors, performance. Never your screen recordings, audio, transcripts, or OCR text. Signed out, events carry only a random device ID. Signed in, they are linked to your account, including your email.
settings.privacy.analytics.description: Usage data, linked to your account when signed in

settings.privacy.remoteLogs.title: Remote support logs
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.unresolved.e: Could not verify whether this device is managed. Remote log controls stay locked and will retry automatically.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.unresolved.c: Checking whether remote log collection is managed by your organization...
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.managed.desc: Your organization can request diagnostic logs from this managed device. Nothing is uploaded unless an administrator sends a request. Logs are filtered locally for common secrets and personal data, but automated filtering can miss secrets and logs can still contain names, file paths, URLs, and error messages. They go to your organization's configured support service, which controls retention. Screenshots, recordings, audio files, chat history, settings, and the timeline database are never included.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.consumer.des: Allow screenpipe support to request recent diagnostic logs from this device. Before upload, logs are filtered locally on this device for common secrets and personal data, but automated filtering can miss secrets and logs can still contain names, file paths, URLs, and error messages. Screenshots, recordings, audio files, chat history, settings, and the timeline database are never included. Nothing is uploaded unless support sends a short-lived request. You can turn this off at any time; previously shared diagnostics are deleted after 30 days.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.status.ready: Consent synced. Support can request one upload while this device is online.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.status.error: Could not reach support. No request will run until the connection recovers; retrying automatically.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.status.signe: The signed-in session is not ready, so no remote request can run.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.status.check: Remote consent is enabled locally; checking the support connection.
settings.privacy.remoteLogs.status.disab: Remote support log collection is disabled.
settings.privacy.filters.apps.descriptio: Switch an app off to stop recording it. Everything else keeps being captured.
settings.privacy.filters.allowlistNotice: An allowlist is active, so only the apps switched on are recorded. Clear the “only capture these” rules below to go back to capturing everything.
settings.privacy.filters.skipWindows.too: Narrower than switching off a whole app. 'Slack::#hr' skips only that channel; '::confidential' skips any window whose title contains the word, in any app.
settings.privacy.filters.onlyCapture.too: Leave empty to capture everything except what you switched off. Adding entries turns capture into an allowlist: 'Slack::#engineering' keeps only that channel of Slack and leaves other apps alone.
When this list is non-empty, browser capture is restricted to matching hostnames. Native apps and tabs whose URL cannot be verified are not recorded.
Block rules take priority over the allowlist. Choose exact domain matching or include its subdomains; optional exceptions stay visible on the rule.

settings.retention.recent.confirmTitle: delete the last {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}?
settings.retention.recent.confirmBody: this permanently removes every screen recording, audio segment, transcription, and ocr capture from the last {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. files are also deleted from disk. this cannot be undone.
settings.retention.lowDisk.title: stop recording before disk is full
settings.retention.lowDisk.description: when free space falls to {threshold}, stop capture and notify you. search, scheduled tasks, and existing data stay available. on by default.
settings.retention.policy.title: storage policy
settings.retention.policy.description: what happens to recordings as they age
settings.retention.current.media: currently: dropping video + audio older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, text stays searchable.
settings.retention.current.lean: currently: dropping video + audio and the bulky ocr/accessibility detail older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, text + memories stay searchable.
settings.retention.current.all: currently: deleting everything older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
settings.retention.mode.off.title: keep everything
settings.retention.mode.off.body: disk keeps growing. you monitor space yourself.
settings.retention.mode.media.title: drop video + audio, keep text
settings.retention.mode.media.body: reclaims mp4/wav/jpeg files. transcripts, ocr, and app history stay searchable. you won't be able to replay clips past the cutoff.
settings.retention.mode.lean.title: trim heavy ui data, keep text + memories
settings.retention.mode.lean.body: everything media mode does, plus drops the bulky per-element ocr + accessibility detail (the biggest part of the database) older than the cutoff. text search, transcripts, timeline, and memories still work — only the on-screen element geometry is dropped. stops the database from ballooning and frees that space for reuse.
settings.retention.mode.all.title: delete everything
settings.retention.mode.all.body: permanently deletes all data past the cutoff. search won't find anything from that period.
settings.retention.cutoff.off: cutoff (applies once a policy is on)
settings.retention.compact.title: reclaim disk space
settings.retention.compact.description: rebuild the database file so freed space goes back to your drive. cleanup keeps the database from growing; compacting is what actually shrinks the file.
settings.retention.compact.needsSpace: needs about {required} free while it runs; you have {available}.
settings.retention.compact.confirmBody: screenpipe will rebuild db.sqlite to return freed space to your drive. recording briefly pauses while it runs, and the data size may temporarily grow before dropping when compaction finishes.
settings.retention.confirm.media.title: enable media eviction?
settings.retention.confirm.lean.title: enable lean cleanup?
settings.retention.confirm.all.title: delete everything past the cutoff?
settings.retention.confirm.media.body: every day, screenpipe will delete video and audio files older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. transcripts, ocr text, and your app/window timeline stay searchable.
settings.retention.confirm.lean.body: every day, screenpipe will reclaim video and audio files and drop the bulky per-element ocr + accessibility detail older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} — the part that makes the database grow. your text search, transcripts, timeline, and memories stay intact. clip replay past the cutoff will not be available.
settings.retention.confirm.all.body1: every day, screenpipe will permanently delete
settings.retention.confirm.all.body2: data older than {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} — recordings, transcripts, ocr, ui events. search will not find anything past that. this cannot be undone.
settings.retention.preview.free1: on your device this would currently free
settings.retention.preview.nothing: nothing past the cutoff right now — first cleanup will run when data ages in.
settings.retention.toast.compactedNothin: already compact — nothing to reclaim right now.
